#166321 348 2006-04-18T22:54:02Z scythe33
Ok, I'll try my hand .
23-0 is pretty simple, just run to the left for the switch, jump the drones, and drop down to the door.
23-1 is a little harder- jump up the column of gold, if you're like me you'll need it for the next few levels, when the bottom drone chases you drop down.
Hit the right launchpad, and jump up the boxes by bouncing off the sides (you might want to practice walljumping now, it's important to learn), then jump in the room with the switch.
Then jump down the boxes, going towards the left, and hit the left launchpad to get the switch.
That should get you to the door.
23-2 is pretty hard, but really just requires timing.
walljump of the first box to get the bottom left switch, then run over and jump on the right box and on to the bottom right switch.
Hit the left launchpad and jump up to the top right switch off the bouncy block, then run and jump to try to get the doorswitch (might take a few tries). Run and jump to get the top right switch, then drop down, and go in the door.
23-3 is easy so long as you got the gold on 23-1, so that you have enough time to take the right path. Just hit the launchpads, stop in the middle of the run at the top. This is cake after the last two.
23-4 ok this level requires one hell of a trick. Drop down onto the middle bounce block, and (time this really good), press right as it starts to spring back up, when the ninja starts moving hit space and if you did it right he should bounce up out of the hole, then just get the door.


Hope that helps, I'm no genius or great player, just posted the paths I took the first time I beat the levels.

I beat Brain n-bolism, in fact its rather easy.
I'll post a demo when I get home (im at school ), but for now I can give you a few hints:
Run to the right at the beginning. Before you get out of the corridor, hit space and hold it and right and hold until you hit the wall. Jump down, and jump over the thwump. Then jump on the top right corner of the bbouncy block to get to the door.
It can take crazy timing in some parts, but it's really not that hard.

#169071 114 2006-04-28T00:55:30Z scythe33
Quote: Markypoo, April 22, 2006 04:56 pm
Hey guys! I'm a long time N player, first time replier. I haven't found any good tutorial websites or documents concerning any N levels, so i figured i would come straight to the source: the forum created by the creators of the game itself. And i seem to have found the thread i am looking for, hopefully this thread is still in operation, as in people that can help are here. I am going for the first flavour and I'm stuck on Ep. 8 Lvl 1: plan plan plan. This level is really freaking hard, and long. A screenshot would be nice, I don't need a crazy long handwritten essay or anything. I just cant sem to come up with a good route plan, and i guess that is why this level is aptly titled; plan plan plan. Does anyone have a good plan plan plan for me?

-Mark

Sure... 8-1's not that hard.
Before you get the switch in the chaingun box, drop down in the floorguard's little couloir and have him chase you to the right side. Bounce in and out of the chainguns, and jump up the left wall. Get the gold in the box (you'll need it), and drop down the right hole in the part on the left and run like mad to the right wall.
Drop down and run for the switch, then back, before the floorguard hits you, then up, and down the column you opened with the switches. Jump immediately to let the floorguard pass, then slide down the left wall and climb back up to get the other floorguard to the left side. Drop down the right hole and run to the right wall, then, get the drone to chase you while it's along the top of its chamber. Now you have to go quickly, get the door button, and drop down to the passage with the bottom floorguard. Run like mad for the right wall, and jump like mad up the right wall, past the chainguns, and hit the launchpad. If you're moving fast enough, the drone will still be in the hallway where you got the door button, and the launchpad will push you right up to the exit.

First, I'd say wait on 67-4. It's the hardest of the bunch.

It's very tricky, though.
80-4 took me until I had beaten the 70's column and the 50's column to beat. Basically, just go for it, you can't take this slow.
92-1: There's a very simple trick that makes this level much, much easier. Jump to the right, then go to the left, where the door and the switch are.
After the thwumps pass, jump through the oneway platforms and stand under the thwump as it comes back down (but a little to the right). The thwump will push you through the oneway and you can jump right into the door.

#189321 73 2006-06-14T13:56:46Z scythe33
Yeah, but you see, things tend to improve with practice.
The distance along nerve cells from the brain to the muscle which operates the hand is about 1m. The normal range of nerve conduction velocity is about 50-60 m/s, so 1/60th of a second is the amount of time it takes for a signal to go from the brain to a nerve. The distance from the eye to the brain is negligible, about 10 cm, so 1/600th of a second (it can be ignored)
In other words, you are perfectly within your limits to react within 1/20th of a second. You just have to reach them first.

A physicist and a mathematician are sharing a hotel room, and in the middle of the night both are awakened by the smell of smoke a small fire has started in the room. The physicist jumps out of bed, rushes to the kitchen, fills a saucepan with water and throws it over the fire, which fizzles out. The physicist leaves the saucepan, with some water still in it, near their beds in case it is needed again, and both men go back to sleep. Some time later, the mathematician again wakes up to the smell of smoke, but the physicist does not. Once again, a small fire has started in the room. The mathematician jumps out of bed, grabs the saucepan, and takes it back to the kitchen where he empties it and puts it back in the cupboard. He then returns to bed, safe in the knowledge that he has reduced the problem to one already solved.

Normal Door Propulsion: in my experience, it only works with 6 gold on the door-otherwise you leave gold behind or the propulsion fizzles out. It's tough to pull off, and the only way to control it is the speed at which the ninja hits the door.

Bounceblock Propulsion: The easiest way (for me) is to c-snap the gold to the edge of the bounceblock. From there, varying the amount of gold changes the propulsion.

Others: Aside from the Lucidium Effect, seen in Tower Loop, the main I'll mention is from joe_kapow's awesome DDA Immortal, which was sniped off the top rated page so it's unlikely that you've seen it. Anyway, simply put, lord_day's proof is heuristically correct, but not rigorous.
However, if you want another one...
0.999~
=
9*sum(k=1 to infty)[(1/10)^k]
which is a geometric series.
By a well-known theorem,
sum(k=1 to infty)[x^k] = x/(1-x) = 1/(1/x - 1)
so the equation becomes
9* (1/(10-1))
= 9*(1/9)
=1
quod erat demonstradtum
That avoids messy infinity minus one debates.

#195084 80 2006-06-27T00:21:22Z scythe33
I suppose my first post in this thread didn't make sense. If you want an exact proof, you have to go about it with limits.
You can't simply define a number as 0.99~ with infinity nines, because infinity isn't a number.
So, 0.99~ is defined as the limit of the sequence
{0, 0.9, 0.99, 0.999, ... , (1-(1/10)^n)}
at infinity. The sequence is equivalent to the function 1 - (1/10)^x.
By the definition of a limit, the limit L of a function at infinity (assuming the function is monotone increasing or decreasing, which this function is) is any number such that given a number δ > 0, there exists an ε such that |L - f(ε)| < δ. For any given δ > 0, set ε to be -log(δ) + 1. Then |1 - f(ε)| = 1 - (1 - (1/10)^(-log(δ) + 1)) = δ/10 < δ.
Since there exists an ε for all given δ > 0, 1 is indeed the limit of the function as it goes to infinity, and 0.99~ is equal to 1.
Now I can say quod erat demonstradtum.

#9834 1 2006-07-01T03:10:00Z scythe33
This isn't by me, if I haven't made that clear enough already, but the author said I could post it here.
I thought you all might like it, that's all.

Silent evening- Venomium

Your words causing my delirium.
Good and Evil no longer in equilibrium.
Were alone, were not together,
Without that, what does is matter?
The guitar tunes echoed in my head, while the words sprang from my lips. We are a good team, John and me. His play, my text. It sounded even better then; in the shadows of evening, shadows which were being driven by the campfire. Our friends listened to us; Mirande, with her eyes closed, a smile on her lips, her head resting on my shoulder. Olivia on Mikes lap, silently mumbling the words of the song, spilling beer on Mikes knee, and Mike, slightly drunk, stroking Olivia, while staring in the swirling flames.
Allow me to get through to you,
Down in the gloom,
Love lurking, our bringer of doom.
I love you, you love me,
Why can't we see that this is simply meant to be?
John smiled, and looked at Jennifer, his hands delivering the sounds caged within the guitar, while the melody caressed our ears. He partly turned and looked straight at me. I could see the question he wanted to ask, burning in his eyes: "When will you make your move? She's alone, and cold. Youre singing, but not acting. Do something, do something now!"
I looked at Jennifer and was amazed again that she had no boyfriend; greenish, sparkling eyes, long blonde hair, softer than silk, red carveless lips, never touched, never desacrated.
Innocent as one could be, unfortunately, just as naive.
I saw Olivia watching me, mumbling the song as I sung the last words, and she saw me observing Jennifer. Her expression was like a book; "Come on, take your chance, give her something to drink, make her drunk."

Olivia is Jennifers best friend, yet not that innocent.

The flames increased, their heat embraced us all and we gladly accepted it. Time began to pass, darkness tightened, and the shadows multiplied. Our fire, a beacon in the cold, chilling grasp of blackness. Our fire, representing our friendship, through the darkest of times.
Time flies when youre having fun. Or when youre drunk. I smiled and closed my eyes while taking another nip of my Vodka.
A few moments later I had to stand up to take a piss, knowing that when I got back, I could go and sit next to Jennifer... Why not? We were a little drunk, both of us and something might happen. It just might...
I went and when I got back, I tried to make it look as casual as possible, but John grinned, and could barely contain the joke he wanted to make. Giving him an angry look, I thought by myself: I'm here, now start talking, idiot!
She rested her head on my shoulder, the soft, long hair covered the entire left side of my body. It smelled like the image of a blue, little waterfall, stroking in the midst of a beautiful spring forest. A white rose amongst red, an oasis in the desert.
I put my arm around her, gave her a sip of my drink and smiled. Her soft body curled up to me, her mysterious eyes closed and her mouth uttered soft words, barely recognizable: "Could you sing for me?" Her eyes slowly opened, carrying a soft sparkle. Of hope? Of love? I didn't know, but what I did know was that I had to do what she asked of me.
"Sure, what song would you like to hear?"
She placed her hand on my chest and lay her legs partly over mine. "About that girl, you know, the second you sang this night."
Angels in the sky,
Never free without their price,
their perfection.

The purest crystal,
The flawless ruby,
The light in darkness,
You.
I started to improvise, I was so close to her ear, I got dazed by her smell, her softness, her touch...
Ocean eyes, staring into the void,
waiting for something, waiting for someone,
perhaps even waiting for me.
Know that I'll be here for you,
Always and ever.

Your blonde hair,
Waiting to be touched,
Your soft lips,
Waiting to be kissed...
She turned to me, her eyes wide open and then, she kissed me.
Her right hand in my hair, her left stroking my back. Her lips against mine, her tongue melting with mine.
I was exalted; her lips, her nose, her face, so close, so real, with me, for me!
I couldnt believe this, where we finally together?
Our kiss slowly ended, we were both smiling, in her arms I felt free.



I awoke, another school day began. Another day, without her. Her death, two years ago, still touches me.

#199684 2 2006-07-06T21:42:24Z scythe33
Sadly, this level doesn't really allow for a diagram. Here's the tips from Aries Easy Way:
Quote: t3h ub3r 1337 Aries
Ok, so for 69-2, Apoplexy, there is no 'easy way' so all I can do is give you tips, because I can talk about doing certain routes, but if you don't do timing exactly as I say, things become very hard. Plus it's hard for me to describe.

So I'm going to split the level into three horizontal pieces and give tips on each piece.

First piece is easy, don't kill yourself on the mines, and don't worry about getting all the gold.

Second part is tricky, just get past the first drone by luring or being quick getting by him. If you can, lure drones to the left part of this section to get them out of the way for a bit. I recommend making big jumps across this section and getting it done quickly, because you've got a fair amount of room to land on the flat angled part of each jagged part.

The third part is harder, so take your time. The drones basically can be moving left or right at two heights, so it's pretty easy to dodge them if you take your time. The key is getting detected when they're moving left to right, and that way they will race right over your head while you chill in the little spaces below them. I should note that you can run from left to right off the angled sections and you will clear the mines and not trigger the drones if they are moving along to top of this section. If you don't lure them left or right, and you're in the middle, there's a good chance one will come down on you at an inopportune moment. Either way, take your time and make your way from one side to the other and back. You can land on either side of the mines, as long as you're careful.

Once you're out of there, you need to come back across the second part. This is hard. There are probably a few drones hanging around, and it's hard enough to make your way across as is. I recommend not worrying too much about luring drones unless you're pretty confident. Also, I definitely recommend trying to land on the flat angled parts (to the right side of each mine) because you have to pretty skilled to keep your momentum from sending you into the mine if you land to the left of it, and the faster you're going, the harder it is to survive landing on the left side of a mine. There really is a good amount of luck in this part, because depending on how you lured drones and got through the level, you could end up with a lot of drones or one or two drones. So just work on doing it fairly quickly, but don't kill yourself on a mine.

The last part is easy. You can really just hold right (as long as you clear the first mine) and you can run straight to the exit, because running up the slopes will give you enough momentum to get over the mines. At this point, you probably don't want to screw anything up, because this is a HARD level.

That's all for 69-2. That was the hardest level for me to beat, and it really requires skill and a dash of luck.

As for 55-0, the ringer, in the drone section you can do a few things to make life easier on yourself. I thought this level was really hard the first time I did it, but it really isn't that bad once you realize that when the drones race after you, you control them. You can force them to go away from you or where you want. To start, you can try to lure some to the lower part of the level just to get them out of the way for a moment. That's fine, but don't focus on luring, focus on getting up the level and lure as you go. What you'll see as far as drone patterns go is that they will probably be going right and left in sort of a zigzag pattern downwards. If they are going upwards, then it should be easy to avoid them or lure them away. Anyways. If they are coming down, and you're going up, what's going to happen is they will be coming in a straight line towards you a little bit higher up than you as you are trying to jump from one side to the other. You can take care of them in one of two ways: the first is to jump over them, which can be done, but is harder, or you can just jump straight up and lure them towards you, then jump from one side to the other once they're far enough over.

You should be able to do this pretty easily and work your way up towards the top. Once you near the top, try to lure a few drones up towards the top, because once you hit the last switch, the drones can get into the little room with the door, and that complicates things. So make your way down while the drones are zipping about, and if did your luring right (to the bottom at the beginning, to the top near the end) then the way to the exit shouldn't be too difficult.

That's all for 55-0, and that finishes my post on tips for apoplexy and the ringer. Remember that when drones are involved, a lot of the time you need to work on luring them around, and luck and skill are what you need to rely on more than an 'easy' route.

#202421 136 2006-07-14T01:36:07Z scythe33
Here's a guide for 69-2, made by Aries himself:
Ok, so for 69-2, Apoplexy, there is no 'easy way' so all I can do is give you tips, because I can talk about doing certain routes, but if you don't do timing exactly as I say, things become very hard. Plus it's hard for me to describe.

So I'm going to split the level into three horizontal pieces and give tips on each piece.

First piece is easy, don't kill yourself on the mines, and don't worry about getting all the gold.

Second part is tricky, just get past the first drone by luring or being quick getting by him. If you can, lure drones to the left part of this section to get them out of the way for a bit. I recommend making big jumps across this section and getting it done quickly, because you've got a fair amount of room to land on the flat angled part of each jagged part.

The third part is harder, so take your time. The drones basically can be moving left or right at two heights, so it's pretty easy to dodge them if you take your time. The key is getting detected when they're moving left to right, and that way they will race right over your head while you chill in the little spaces below them. I should note that you can run from left to right off the angled sections and you will clear the mines and not trigger the drones if they are moving along to top of this section. If you don't lure them left or right, and you're in the middle, there's a good chance one will come down on you at an inopportune moment. Either way, take your time and make your way from one side to the other and back. You can land on either side of the mines, as long as you're careful.

Once you're out of there, you need to come back across the second part. This is hard. There are probably a few drones hanging around, and it's hard enough to make your way across as is. I recommend not worrying too much about luring drones unless you're pretty confident. Also, I definitely recommend trying to land on the flat angled parts (to the right side of each mine) because you have to pretty skilled to keep your momentum from sending you into the mine if you land to the left of it, and the faster you're going, the harder it is to survive landing on the left side of a mine. There really is a good amount of luck in this part, because depending on how you lured drones and got through the level, you could end up with a lot of drones or one or two drones. So just work on doing it fairly quickly, but don't kill yourself on a mine.

The last part is easy. You can really just hold right (as long as you clear the first mine) and you can run straight to the exit, because running up the slopes will give you enough momentum to get over the mines. At this point, you probably don't want to screw anything up, because this is a HARD level.

nice map 4.5
btw have you been giving me bad ratings for my maps(not accusing)

Quote: AMomentLikeThis
I only rate maps what I think they deserve, if I don't like a map I usually don't rate it or give some advice

---

Now a little while ago I decide to check Numa (finding that one of my recent tilesets has a 0 with 1 vote), and this map:

Quote: LikeNike99
the map is dum for a reason. i have proff that

because of this i deleted all my maps
everysingle 1 of my 4.5 maps wer turned into a 3 or 3.5 by him ]2and maybe his mates

lmao

Thank you for reading, and I hope you don't think I'm a liar, if so then I guess my place is obviously not on Numa.

Quote: aries easy way
Ok, so for 69-2, Apoplexy, there is no 'easy way' so all I can do is give you tips, because I can talk about doing certain routes, but if you don't do timing exactly as I say, things become very hard. Plus it's hard for me to describe.

So I'm going to split the level into three horizontal pieces and give tips on each piece.

First piece is easy, don't kill yourself on the mines, and don't worry about getting all the gold.

Second part is tricky, just get past the first drone by luring or being quick getting by him. If you can, lure drones to the left part of this section to get them out of the way for a bit. I recommend making big jumps across this section and getting it done quickly, because you've got a fair amount of room to land on the flat angled part of each jagged part.

The third part is harder, so take your time. The drones basically can be moving left or right at two heights, so it's pretty easy to dodge them if you take your time. The key is getting detected when they're moving left to right, and that way they will race right over your head while you chill in the little spaces below them. I should note that you can run from left to right off the angled sections and you will clear the mines and not trigger the drones if they are moving along to top of this section. If you don't lure them left or right, and you're in the middle, there's a good chance one will come down on you at an inopportune moment. Either way, take your time and make your way from one side to the other and back. You can land on either side of the mines, as long as you're careful.

Once you're out of there, you need to come back across the second part. This is hard. There are probably a few drones hanging around, and it's hard enough to make your way across as is. I recommend not worrying too much about luring drones unless you're pretty confident. Also, I definitely recommend trying to land on the flat angled parts (to the right side of each mine) because you have to pretty skilled to keep your momentum from sending you into the mine if you land to the left of it, and the faster you're going, the harder it is to survive landing on the left side of a mine. There really is a good amount of luck in this part, because depending on how you lured drones and got through the level, you could end up with a lot of drones or one or two drones. So just work on doing it fairly quickly, but don't kill yourself on a mine.

The last part is easy. You can really just hold right (as long as you clear the first mine) and you can run straight to the exit, because running up the slopes will give you enough momentum to get over the mines. At this point, you probably don't want to screw anything up, because this is a HARD level.

Well, I'm more intimate with this subject that anyone on this forum, I imagine. My life has been a series of existential crises (mine and others') strung together. Two of my close family members committed suicide--another died of natural causes when I was younger. My brother went just recently. Had something to do with genetics, I think. Also, death seems to be our fixation. It was mine for a while, and then I got over it. I was a washed out druggy who viewed his life as a jaded existence devoid of any vertical social movement. Now, I'm a content alcoholic whose life is chock full of lateral social movement. It's all a matter of perspective--and I couldn't be happier now. "No", says the clerk, "we only sell dog food and cat food."
"OK", says the duck and walks out.
The next day the duck walks in the store and says "Uh, got any duck food?"
The clerk once again replies, "No, like I told you, we only sell cat food and dog food."
"OK", says the duck and walks out.
The next day the duck walks in the store and says "Uh, got any duck food?"
The clerk says "Hey look, I told you two times already that we only sell cat food and dog food!"
"OK", says the duck and walks out.
The next day the duck walks in the store and says "Uh, got any duck food?"
This time the clerk yells "We don't sell any duck food and if you come in here one more time asking, I am going to nail your little webbed feet to the ground!"
"OK", says the duck and walks out.
The next day the duck walks in the store and says "Uh, got any nails?"
"No", says the confused clerk.
The duck says, "Got any duck food?"

#239676 67 2006-10-11T19:27:01Z scythe33
Quote: Baraba, October 08, 2006 08:46 pm
Say you have a box, just a plain unassuming box. And someone casually asks you to, through logic, decide what is inside the box. Your first thought is that it's most logical to assume nothing is in the box because that's the most apparent. There's no real evidence to the contrary so why not? But then, there's no evidence to support that conclusion either. There could be something inside of it. You can't prove that there isn't. So you turn to the inquirer and say: "I don't know if anything is in the box and I certainly have no clue as to the nature of the 'thing' that could possibly lie within."
Another person walks up and says: " I couldn't help but overhear your conversation. I believe that it's actually most logical to assume there is nothing within the box."
Someone else cries out that, yes, there is most definitely something inside of it.
So, which is the most rational conclusion: The box is empty, the box is not empty, or it's impossible to tell whether or not it is empty?

Well, seeing as you are given no other information, all possible outcomes have an equal probability, no?
Naturally, nothing is one possible outcome, say, a pencil is another, a stapler, hair, cheese, etc. In fact, there are infinitely many possible outcomes, each, by the original assumption, having equal probability. The probability that there is nothing in the box is thus one outcome in infinitely many possible outcomes, or zero, so we can conclude that with a probability of one, there is something in the box.
All speaking theoretically of course.

#265686 23 2006-12-06T23:11:17Z scythe33
Quote: Aries Easy Way
This is one of my all-time favorite levels, I think the map is well made and it shows. The key to this level is simple: you better have skill, and don't screw up. Seriously, this is a tough level to beat consistently, so keep trying, because you get better at doing each individual piece of the level the more you do it. Which brings me to how I'm going to attack this level. There are six groups of gold with a switch in it, and it doesn't really matter in what order you do them in, they may as well be separate mini-levels that you have to do consecutively. I'm going to list each seperately in the order I think is easiest in overall terms (get the tough stuff out of the way first is best in my opinion).

First section: The mines in the lower right.
Really, all this section is about is navigating the mines and jumping precisely. Pure skill once you know the way. My suggested route to get back up and out of this part sends you back to where you started, but you can do it the other way, you're just a bigger gauss target.

Second section: The drones and mines.
Well the drones follow a set pattern, so just drop in between them, or when one of them is in the lower right corner, drop to where he is (he'll move and you'll be set to grab the switch and wall jump out of there easily). Shouldn't be too bad if you see what's going on and realize the spacing of the mines is not bad at all.

Third section: The switch at the top, next to a wall, with mines above and below.
Note that when you're getting up here, you have to make a big wall jump across the main portion of the level that's easily screwed up if you're not experienced. Getting to the actual switch is no problem. Either jump from the lip of the pipe down and to the left of the switch, or wall jump off the lip of the pipe up to the switch. Then wall jump off to either the lip of the pipe down and to the left, or onto the curve in the pipe to the left.

Fourth Section: The switch with a floorguard under it.
Be cognizant of the floor guards on the way here. Remember this is the final level of the episode, so time is not an issue. This part itself is really not too bad of a reflex thing, just drop in the middle and jump right away and you can do it, or you can lure the floorguard to the side to buy yourself more time. Grab the switch, and don't step on the floorguard or mines. Just jump as soon as you hit the ground and you'll be fine.

Note - Getting down from there can be tricky, either wallslide the vertical mouth of the pipe or jump off the mouth to the vertical mouth down by the mines, or you could walljump from the upper left vertical mouth to the other side wall, the reverse of the way you got here.

Fifth Section: The switch guarded by thwumps.
The easy way to do this part is to drop from the lip by where you started and fall hard right, so you land on top of the thwumps. They'll move out of the way, then jump over them to the middle over top of them as they come back. As soon as they both trigger a second time, jump and get the switch. Then just jump out before the trigger a third time, which shouldn't be too hard, and you'll be fine. You can do this part faster, like having the thwumps trigger only once or twice (you can land on top of them and walk on top of them back out if you're good, like in my highscore). I'm just giving you the way that requires the least precision.

Sixth section: The terminal switch.
Get up to the lip of the pipe that is below this part, jump up to the wall, wall jump to the switch, and waltz to the door. Just don't get killed by the gauss turret.

For the diagram, the red line is the way to the switch(notice that the third switch has two routes to the switch I drew up because both work fine), the blue line is the way to relative safety, and the green lines are different ways out (which work just fine, they're just not the routes I use most often).
[/easy way]
Yes, I'm lazy. But Aries is really really good.

My worldview is closest to empirical agnostic atheism, also known as "negative agnosticism" and "weak agnosticism". I have not been given reason to believe that the existence of gods is more or less likely than the alternative. Therefore, I consider the most rational stance is to withhold judgment. I also consider that the probability of any specific religion being reasonably accurate is quite small. I do not pretend to know what happens after death, other than the obvious physical effects. I have some leanings towards apathetic agnosticism (the contention that whether gods exist or not is largely academic and irrelevant to daily life). I've never really felt that gods influence my life; they exist, they appear to be largely uninterested in me, or at the very least have a policy of non-interference.

I do not claim to know why the universe exists. However, once it *did* exist, I believe it (mostly) adhered to certain physical laws, which we have modelled through scientific means. I therefore think that, more likely than not, the universe as we know it expanded from a point about 13 billion years ago. I consider everything beyond this point speculation; you can say it appeared spontaneously or that God created it, but I don't think you can prove either.

I am a moral relativist. I judge what is ethical based on the ramifications not only of individual actions, but the underlying reasons or philosophy. For example, while enforcing the law may not have the most desirable consequences in a specific case, in the long term laws must be applied consistently if people are to respect and understand them. I also recognise that, as a human, I have ingrained sentimental tendencies, and that my judgments are unlikely to be totally objective. It is my opinion that such tendencies likely developed as a mechanism which encourages cooperation between humans, and thus increases their chances of survival, in accordance with the principles of selection.

Quote: blue_tetris, December 14, 2006 04:20 pm
Do trains really have a dead man's handle for a brake? I think that would be unsafe.

Yeah.
Ok, here's a problem with alot of your answers: The fly never "touches" the train-in quantum mechanics, I don't recall any mention of anything "touching".
Rather, the electrons in the fly repel the electrons on the front of the train. Even if the fly were incompressible, it wouldn't matter. He's not in an internal frame of reference, so the idea that his velocity is the same as that of the ground doesn't work-the train is still moving towards him, and is not stopped.
However, the fly doesn't have to stop the train-it already is. Since each inertial frame of reference is as good as any other, the train is already "stopped" in the 100 mph ground velocity frame of reference. The only time something can't be considered "stopped" is while it's accelerating. So, yes, the fly "stops" the already "stopped" train.

Don't bother with highscores on this level. They're pretty crazy.
Also, maps arent of much help either. A few things to keep in mind are:
* Go quickly. The drones aren't as fast as you
* Move diagonally. It keeps them from seeing you.
* Go up the left wall. Well, it worked for me
* Get down quick (but don't run into anything)
* the "triple jump thingy": When between a wall and one of the bounceblocks, tap jump three times fast. It's a good way of getting up, and should keep you out of the way of mines and drones.
* Don't piss yourself off: it sucks! and your playing decreases too. If you're getting angry, go do something else.
* Watch the mines-to me, it didn't take much to get a feel for the drones, but the mines killed me alot.

Oh, and I can't believe you people. "Watch the highscores" isn't very helpful

Quote: Arachnid, 2006-12-18T07:51:43Z
Basing who can vote on an average rating of 2.5 or above, or in any way preferring people who vote high, is a bad idea. 2.5 _should_ be the average vote
This seems intrinsically off. If we define 2.5 as what an "average" map would get, the actual voting average would be higher than 2.5.
An obvious example of this is maps you can tell are bad by the thumbnail, and don't bother looking at. This cuts off a lot of your "zero" votes. If your average (given out) rating would be 2.5 if you rated everything, it moves above 2.5 since you're "cutting out the bottom", so to speak. It wouldn't make sense to try and change this new average back to 2.5-then, the rating you'd give the aforementioned "average" map would be less than 2.5, not 2.5.

An extreme example of this would be if, say, I only rate maps by formica and astheoceansblue. Chances are, the average rating i'd be giving out would be somewhere around 4.3, if I rate an "average" map 2.5. If I lower my average to 2.5, I end up rating an average map 0.2, which certainly isn't fair.
(the numbers are all averages)

#273698 3 2006-12-20T02:14:54Z scythe33
Quote: aries_griff aka 1337ness
I have to really emphasize that this level, more than anything, takes a lot of SKILL.

(Aries's Easy Way)
88-4, Mother Thwumping (Thumping) Impossible, MTI for short.

Ok, the first part (the top) is pretty simple, just don't get killed on the mines. I recommend getting the switch, but it's not actually necessary; you can run through that top part(just hold right all the way and you'll get it) and bounce off the ledge(right by where the platform would appear) and if you have your momentum going, you'll bounce right over the mines. Oh, and watch out for the drone. Easy enough, I shouldn't have to explain anything about it if you've made it this far in the game.

I'll do the rest of this thwump by thwump, or corridor by corridor(where a corridor is like one straight section that ends when the level turns)

The very first thwump is easy. Just jump straight at it, and it will go down, and you will go over. I try to aim to land on the small flat ledge a little to the right of the first thwump.

Standing on that ledge triggers a thwump to come upwards towards you. Don't worry about it, there's enough room on the left side for you to fall safely while it's coming at you. So go ahead and tiptoe off the right side of the ledge and fall straight down. If you fall straight off the ledge and don't move either direction, the thwump will pass you, and you will land on a slanted ledge which will send you to the right side of the corridor onto another slanted ledge that will send you right on top of another thwump(it faces left). So for that falling part, just fall straight off that little ledge(you may have to realign yourself by tapping left once or twice) and don't press anything til you hit that slant that's about 45 degrees in the lower right corner that shoots you on top of the thwump(if all went right). At that point(and maybe a little before you hit the ledge), start moving left. *Alternatively*, if you're not planning to run on top of the thwump in the bottom left, you can take this part a little slower, dropping from ledge to ledge and land in the bottom right where it's safe, so you can get ready for your slow trek across the bottom(I don't like that way).

Start moving left because I found the easiest way to do this part is to just keep running on top of the thwump(really not that hard after the first or second try and it flows really well). Then jump before the thwump coming at you kills you (you should be jumping right after the first of two arches of gold). There should be a raised part in the ceiling right there for you to clear the oncoming thwump, and a flat, raised ledge(with no mines on it) for you to land on. From that ledge, you have to either teeter over the edge(so the ninja isn't standing straight up) or actually be on the slant to jump safely, because there's an overhanging slanted ceiling to block your jump(and send you into the mines) if you jump too high. You should land on a slant that faces towards you, so jump once you land on it or run left off of it, or you'll slide into a mine. So land on that flat part, or the slant next to the mine(you may have landed on them anyways if you jumped far enough), which are right next to the slight slant that faces right, which is where you landed, and jump left. I like to land on the right side of the piece of the floor that kinda looks like a ^ sign and jump into the little crevice above that big vertical piece of wall. You can chill there or wallslide/jump/wallslide that wall below it for a bit if you need to catch your breath, just don't get squashed by a thwump coming back. *ALTERNATIVELY*, if you're shy about riding thwumps, the bottom part is doable just jumping through, it's just tricky. But if you're not riding on top of the thwumps, I would recommend riding on the side of the thwump that comes at you. You can do this by letting it come at you while you chill in the mine-less bottom right corner. Once it hits the wall, jump and wallslide its left side, and keep jumping and holding right, and you should be able to ride the sucker all the way to the little crevice. It takes awhile, but you should have plenty of time.

The decision is how to do this next part. Some people will jump off, land on the slant facing the wall on the ^ shaped part, jump to the wall, wall jump up, then wall jump the teeny vertical ledges. Personally, I always thought that was hard. So I like to chill in the little crevice, then hop up onto that baby corner right above it(yes, it's right next to the mines, so watch out). You don't need to stand on the ledge, you can just land the corner and jump immediately before you fall off. When you jump to the right off that corner, a lot of the time you'll have to walljump off that tiny vertical ledge that's there top hop of to the flat ledge, where you can chill. Jump to the next ledge up, and don't worry about the switch(it's useless IMHO). Then jump up to the slanted part right above that ledge and chill.

This next part has a lot of variation, but I'll tell you what I find easiest. Highscorers jump further right and let the thwump go over them while they cut it close on a slant next to a mine, which is very hard, so I don't recommend. I recommend chilling on that slant you are on, above the ledges and hopping and holding right, so the thwump triggers and goes right over your head(with a significant amount of room). Then jump on the right side of the thwump(it's back) and wallslide/jump/wallslide by jumping and holding left the entire time. You can hold on as long as you want, and depending on where you get off the thwump, your strategy changes a little. I like getting off of the thwump somewhere around the terminal switch, and I usually do it by jumping high on one of my wall slide jumps, landing on top of the thwump and jumping so it goes under me(or just clearing it with the first jump). You can do this pretty safely right before or right after the terminal switch(I prefer before, because you have more landing room). Then I wait in that flat area to the right of the terminal(you can wait on any surface you like, just don't get killed, and make sure theres a high ceiling) and when the thwump come back at me, I jump over it, let it go under(I usually land on the 45 degree right facing slant to the right of the terminal) , then make the rest of my jumps. I jump from that 45 degree slant to the next small gap in the mines, a smaller slant that faces left, and then I hop (I think it's safer than a full jump) to the small flat gap between mines. Then I hop over to the slanted corner and wait(hop and wait, so I don't fall immediately).

This next part(next 2 corridors) is extremely difficult, and there's no way around it that I found. My favorite way to do it is very hard, but so is every other way. You have to trigger that thwump facing upwards by leaning over the edge or hopping. Then when it hits the top, fall off the ledge under it. There are three slants you can land on, and each has a way to survive.

This is where it gets extremely difficult. You can pick which ledge to land on, I'll explain each, and I'll put a number for each so you can know when I talk about each. I like to land on the ledge on the left (the steepest one), so I'll start by explaining that.
(*1*) When you fall, land directly on the ledge, which will require a little steering, because if you fall straight down, you won't be far enough left to hit it. With the momentum of your fall, jump as soon as you hit the ledge, which is very hard, and then land in the small gap between mines (there's a flat part and a slanted part, but it's tough to land in that area because of the speed). Depending on how fast you were going and where you jump from, you will 9 times out of ten need to hold right to slow down your jump so you don't overshoot that small gap. Then jump immediately when you land to avoid the thwump coming from the left straight at you. You can jump straight up and come back down or you can jump up and left to the next piece of floor clear of mines, which is three mines away from where you landed. From there, just keep jumping from one small clearing to another til you are on that ledge at the end of the corridor(the jumps are hard, I know, but there's nothing I can do to help you with that). *Alternatively*, once you jump over the thwump that comes from the left side towards you, you can wait til it comes back and ride the left side of it to the ledge like I have previously described.
(*2*) Landing on the slant on the far right instead of the slant I talked about earlier is much the same. I don't like it because you have to watch out for the mines to even get to the slant to land on it, and once you land on it, the jump is harder. Anyways, once you land on the small slant on the right, do the exact jump as I described earlier, to the gap between a set of 3 mines and a set of 4 mines. Only now, the jump is farther. I have done this, so I know it is possible, but I think it's harder (personal opinion).
(*3*) The middle ledge. You might think it's easier, because you don't have to jump right when you land on it, and for some it will be. Since you can't jump left with enough speed to beat the thwump coming towards you when you land in the middle, your only choice is to wait for the thwumps to come to you. On the other ledges, you didn't have to worry about when the timing with vertical thwump coming back down, but for this one it may make a big difference. The idea for this ledge is to wait for the vertical thwump to come back down, and jump up and left off your ledge into that little gap between the mine and the vertical thwump before it traps you. If you wait for the vertical thwump at the top of the descent, so that when you fall to this middle ledge, you barely beat the thwump coming back down(so you are pretty close to getting smashed between the corner you fall from and the thwump coming back down), if you do that, what happens is that the vertical thwump is closer to resetting when the thwump coming from the left triggers. This allows you enough time to trigger the vertical thwump again by jumping up and left(you may like to jump to the left-facing 45 degree slant to left of the middle slant to prevent being trapped) and so when that vertical thwump triggers for the second time, the left-right thwump goes underneath you. Then you can either ride that thwump over to the ledge on the left side of the corner, or wait in one of the safe parts and let it go under you, or you can go faster through this horizontal corridor than the thwump does coming back. The point is, if you can delay the thwump coming from the left triggering, it makes this easier, and the basic idea is get the vertical thwump out of the corner and make it so you don't have to deal with that thwump coming fast at you from the left. It's a tricky jump triggering the vertical thwump from that lower right corner so that the left-right thwump doesn't kill you, but you may find it easier than executing the jumps from the other ledges.

Any way you do that last part, it's probably going to be very hard, and you end up on the small ledge on the left part of the corridor. This vertical corridor is small and nothing happens in it, so I recommend gathering your thoughts and focusing for the last part, which is hard. Just jump your way to that top small slant that faces right, and get ready.

The last part is the most intense. You start from that little slant at the start of the corridor(the thwump won't trigger yet, so don't worry). The next jumps are precision jumps that require skill and speed. From that slant, jump to the SECOND gap in the mines (theres a piece of gold over each gap). The second one is MUCH easier to hit for me, and it makes clearing the thwump easy. The thwump triggers as you land, so from that second gap, jump high and to the right a little, and follow the ceiling to land in the last gap in the mines. Then jump high and to the right again, and follow the ceiling again right to the door. Congrats, you made it!

[/easy way]
Memorize it. You will so be tested on Friday. 30 multiple choice questions, and an essay on why searching is important.

#277789 78 2006-12-28T00:32:16Z scythe33
I have another ratings idea!
Count the number of people who have voted a certain amount by it's square for the averaging.
I.E. a map is 5'd by three people, so as far as the average is concerned, it got 5'd by nine people. That way, 3 5s and 1 0 would average to
(9*5 + 1*0)/(9+1) = 4.5
instead of
(3*5 + 1*0)/(3+1) = 3.9
That wouldn't eliminate a person's ability to rate a map what they think it deserves, but it should make a dent in the effectiveness of sniping.

#277843 53 2006-12-28T03:29:06Z scythe33
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cantor%27s_diagonal_argument

Heh. There are an infinite number of "cardinalities", which roughly speaking means the size of an infinite set.
Assuming the generalized continuum hypothesis
The integers, as that implies, have cardinality aleph-null
The real numbers have cardinality aleph-one.
Now, the set of holomorphic functions on the unit disk has a bijection with the set of sequences of real numbers that are not exponentially increasing, and so by that same diagonal argument, the set of holomorphic functions on the unit disk has cardinality aleph-two.
Naturally, there are an infinite number of integers, an infinite number of real numbers, and an infinite number of holomorphic functions, but we can say that one infinity is "bigger" than another.
Obby, your two infinities are equal, btw.

Quote: macaddict, 2007-01-05T21:45:28Z
I believe that the original idea was that Natural selection removes information. And your argument is that Mutations increase information? Sorry, Im not meaning to talk about mutations for this argument. Natural selection can only remove information, sometimes entire alleles, because all it can do is kill off certain genotypes.
You have to realize you're using two different definitions of information, claiming they're equivalent, and then saying that proves your point. Natural selection, like all other processes, increases "information entropy" in the sense that after several hundred thousand years of mutation and natural selection, it's more difficult to figure out what you started with. It does not, however, decrease the complexity of the protein, and the entropy requirement for this is more than compensated for by the biological processes of the animal that is evolving (eating, breathing, etc, are far less than 100% efficient) Only the mutations that improve a protein occur, and there are just about always mutations that do so. As an (amazing!) example, the protein that regulates language differs by just 3 amino acids in humans and chimpanzees, and yet the improvement is astounding. The sickle cell hemoglobin that confers total malaria immunity differs by just one amino acid. There are plenty of other examples.

Quote: macaddict, 2007-01-03T21:42:07Z
Finally, we agree on something. Dog breeding is very similar to natural selection. If I prove to you that the breeding of dogs involves no new information (in the form of alleles), then will you finally get it? I swear, its like talking to a brick wall.

Lets say we have a set of mutts. The mutts have very different DNA, some having alleles for long hair, some short. Some are big, some are small. Some are brown, black, white, spotted, etc. If we artificially select big, hairy dogs, it is done by removing those dogs with short hair and small size from the breeding population. Natural selection could possibly do the job by the need to stay warm in a cold environment.
Now comes the important part: The population has less information because it has less alleles. You'd agree that two essays which differ only in that one of them lacks a paragraph which the other has, the one with one less paragraph has less information & less meaning. The dog populations now lack both the short-hair alleles and the small size alleles.
This is why micro-evolution/natural selection doesn't progress evolution. It is precisely because we lose alleles in the process. The loss of these alleles may prevent interbreeding, which may cause us to call them different species. (How could a Great Dane mate with a Poodle? Sometimes this is enough to have scientists call them different species)
You're the brick wall. Mutations make new alleles throughout the whole process, you know that as well as I do. If it's good, it stays, if it's bad, it doesn't. For example, look at this sequence:

a_{n+1} = a_n + 1 (5% chance)
a_{n+1} = a_n (90% chance)
a_{n+1} = a_n - 1 (5% chance)
Chances are, this will oscillate randomly. Now let's say we remove all of the third case, which is similar to what dog breeding does. The new sequence, with a 5.26% chance of the first case, and a 94.74% chance of the second still exhibits random behavior, but it increases. In other words, we keep the "big" alleles, lose the "small" alelles, and then keep the "bigger" alleles that arise through mutation, and now we've done something. The reason it works is that a "big" allele has more chance of turning into a "bigger" allele (which is what we want) than does a "small" allele, or so we assume (and turn out to be right!)

Quote: macaddict, 2007-01-04T21:45:47Z
I sure hope you're not saying what I think you're saying. Because if you are actually suggesting that there are more proteins than English sentences, you are dead wrong. Example: For any protein you name, I can make many many true sentences and many many false sentences.

"RNA Transcriptase is a brand of baseball glove"
"RNA Transcriptase is an enzyme used by bacteria"
etc, etc.

There are also other large problems about your argument. While there may possibly be many proteins, they are all very different, and few have similar sequences unless they do almost the exact same thing. Also, there are an infinite amount of non-functional proteins, because at a certain point, the polypeptide chain would be too large. The idea that some mutations are helpful deals only with phenotype. For the individual molecule, it is harmful 99% of the time and neutral 1% of the time. And top scientists like Gould affirm that "...virtually every mutation ever known has been harmful to the organism in some way...". Plus, according to complex systems theory, since the rules for making a functional protein are even more strict than the rules of English, it is, by definition, more difficult to change parts without resulting in a nonsensible protein.

One small argument: If you happen to say that bad proteins can be retained because the phenotype is good, then the protein can no longer be affected by natural selection. The effect is the same no matter whether the protein fails in one spot over another, and the phenotype is what is selected for. Remember, that even in bacteria, the effect is somewhat negative because they waste rescources making too much enzyme (in a natural environment).

And another thing: If a spelling error is such a bad analogy, then why was it used by PBS in their series on evolution?
When will you learn you can't prove things by analogy, unless you prove the analogy? You haven't justified the analogy with anything other that "Oh, it looks right". Sure, it can be used to help teach people, but it can't be used as an actual proof.

Quote: macaddict, 2007-01-22T21:44:18Z
But they can be related to words! Changing that alanine to glycine is like adding a 'u' to 'color'. The meaning is the same, but the spelling is different. Since no advantage is conferred, the mutation can't spread easily.
The reason proteins cannot be related to sentences is simple: Languages are not logical. The individual sound of each letter has nothing to do with the meaning of a word. By a massive contrast, proteins are governed by physical laws. The individual characteristics of each amino acid play a giant role in the properties of the protein. Keratin's strength is due to the fact that cysteine has the ability to form thermally stable disulfide crosslinking with itself. Collagens ability to coil tighter is due to glycine's side chain being a single hydrogen atom. The meaning of "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog" has absolutely nothing to do with the fact that it contains every letter in the English alphabet, and the meaning of "uncopyrightable" has nothing to do with the fact that it never uses a letter twice. Quote: macaddict, 2007-01-22T21:44:18Z
Like I said before, Mr. Brick Wall, I'm not saying there's no such thing as an insertion mutation. I'm saying that the most likely circumstance is that both a_n+1 and a_n-1 are totally non-functional, or less functional as far as their coded-for protein goes.
*sigh*
First, any letter can be changed, duplicated, any two letters can be switched, any letter can flip, or "move" in the sequence as it wishes. It can also be duplicated to appear at any other point in the sequence (i'm going on pure memory here). It's not hard to see how we get from this to any letter being inserted anywhere. a_n + 1 and a_n - 1 do not stand for "insert" and "remove". a_n + 1 means "a mutation that improves the protein", such as removing a beta-lactam binding site on a penicillin binding protein. a_n - 1 means "a mutation that harms the protein", such as a change in amyloid that increases the probability of misfolding. The probabilities I gave are grossly unrealistic, but the idea stands. If we remove all the "bad mutations", we're left with "good mutations", and the protein can only get "better". #13736 1 2007-01-28T01:55:34Z scythe33
Count the number of people who have voted a certain amount by it's square for the averaging.
I.E. a map is 5'd by three people and then sniped, so as far as the average is concerned, it got 5'd by nine people. That way, 3 5s and 1 0 would average to
(9*5 + 1*0)/(9+1) = 4.5
instead of
(3*5 + 1*0)/(3+1) = 3.9
That wouldn't eliminate a person's ability to rate a map what they think it deserves, but it should make a dent in the effectiveness of sniping.
Improvements?

I'm really stuck on level 3 - 3 (Deosil). I'm probably missing something, but for some reason my ninja really speeds up over the first switch and just flies straight into the wall and / or the NAVDrone. When I do, however, manage to throw the switch, I always end up getting killed anyway. Any suggestions?

Well, i'd say take your time (there's gold aplenty), and practice walljumping. You don't have to be sliding on a wall to be able to jump off of it, just close enough for the ninja to reach-this is a common misconception. Another thing is that you don't simply hold the button towards the wall and press the jump button randomly. I'm guessing you have trouble going up and down, so with a little practice on that, this level should be cake.
Also, don't be so cautious around drones. Be bold and make some moves that seem idiotic, it's the only way to learn.
Plus, if you stop holding a directional key while you're in the air, he'll keep going in that direction without accelerating. If you're holding it, that could be your problem.
#291151 443 2007-01-28T22:47:42Z scythe33
Quote: Jake8125, January 28, 2007 09:08 am
thx 4 the help i got past it but now i'm on MTI and NOW i think i need to be institutionalised. i've been on it 4 like hours and the furthest i've been is just past the switch to open the door. help me!

Well, first a bit of background. The "mother" in the name is because it's like your mother-it's a b****. The thumping is because of all the thwumps, and impossible is because... well, you get the point.
(Aries's Easy Way)
88-4, Mother Thwumping (Thumping) Impossible, MTI for short.

Ok, the first part (the top) is pretty simple, just don't get killed on the mines. I recommend getting the switch, but it's not actually necessary; you can run through that top part(just hold right all the way and you'll get it) and bounce off the ledge(right by where the platform would appear) and if you have your momentum going, you'll bounce right over the mines. Oh, and watch out for the drone. Easy enough, I shouldn't have to explain anything about it if you've made it this far in the game.

I'll do the rest of this thwump by thwump, or corridor by corridor(where a corridor is like one straight section that ends when the level turns)

The very first thwump is easy. Just jump straight at it, and it will go down, and you will go over. I try to aim to land on the small flat ledge a little to the right of the first thwump.

Standing on that ledge triggers a thwump to come upwards towards you. Don't worry about it, there's enough room on the left side for you to fall safely while it's coming at you. So go ahead and tiptoe off the right side of the ledge and fall straight down. If you fall straight off the ledge and don't move either direction, the thwump will pass you, and you will land on a slanted ledge which will send you to the right side of the corridor onto another slanted ledge that will send you right on top of another thwump(it faces left). So for that falling part, just fall straight off that little ledge(you may have to realign yourself by tapping left once or twice) and don't press anything til you hit that slant that's about 45 degrees in the lower right corner that shoots you on top of the thwump(if all went right). At that point(and maybe a little before you hit the ledge), start moving left. *Alternatively*, if you're not planning to run on top of the thwump in the bottom left, you can take this part a little slower, dropping from ledge to ledge and land in the bottom right where it's safe, so you can get ready for your slow trek across the bottom(I don't like that way).

Start moving left because I found the easiest way to do this part is to just keep running on top of the thwump(really not that hard after the first or second try and it flows really well). Then jump before the thwump coming at you kills you (you should be jumping right after the first of two arches of gold). There should be a raised part in the ceiling right there for you to clear the oncoming thwump, and a flat, raised ledge(with no mines on it) for you to land on. From that ledge, you have to either teeter over the edge(so the ninja isn't standing straight up) or actually be on the slant to jump safely, because there's an overhanging slanted ceiling to block your jump(and send you into the mines) if you jump too high. You should land on a slant that faces towards you, so jump once you land on it or run left off of it, or you'll slide into a mine. So land on that flat part, or the slant next to the mine(you may have landed on them anyways if you jumped far enough), which are right next to the slight slant that faces right, which is where you landed, and jump left. I like to land on the right side of the piece of the floor that kinda looks like a ^ sign and jump into the little crevice above that big vertical piece of wall. You can chill there or wallslide/jump/wallslide that wall below it for a bit if you need to catch your breath, just don't get squashed by a thwump coming back. *ALTERNATIVELY*, if you're shy about riding thwumps, the bottom part is doable just jumping through, it's just tricky. But if you're not riding on top of the thwumps, I would recommend riding on the side of the thwump that comes at you. You can do this by letting it come at you while you chill in the mine-less bottom right corner. Once it hits the wall, jump and wallslide its left side, and keep jumping and holding right, and you should be able to ride the sucker all the way to the little crevice. It takes awhile, but you should have plenty of time.

The decision is how to do this next part. Some people will jump off, land on the slant facing the wall on the ^ shaped part, jump to the wall, wall jump up, then wall jump the teeny vertical ledges. Personally, I always thought that was hard. So I like to chill in the little crevice, then hop up onto that baby corner right above it(yes, it's right next to the mines, so watch out). You don't need to stand on the ledge, you can just land the corner and jump immediately before you fall off. When you jump to the right off that corner, a lot of the time you'll have to walljump off that tiny vertical ledge that's there top hop of to the flat ledge, where you can chill. Jump to the next ledge up, and don't worry about the switch(it's useless IMHO). Then jump up to the slanted part right above that ledge and chill.

This next part has a lot of variation, but I'll tell you what I find easiest. Highscorers jump further right and let the thwump go over them while they cut it close on a slant next to a mine, which is very hard, so I don't recommend. I recommend chilling on that slant you are on, above the ledges and hopping and holding right, so the thwump triggers and goes right over your head(with a significant amount of room). Then jump on the right side of the thwump(it's back) and wallslide/jump/wallslide by jumping and holding left the entire time. You can hold on as long as you want, and depending on where you get off the thwump, your strategy changes a little. I like getting off of the thwump somewhere around the terminal switch, and I usually do it by jumping high on one of my wall slide jumps, landing on top of the thwump and jumping so it goes under me(or just clearing it with the first jump). You can do this pretty safely right before or right after the terminal switch(I prefer before, because you have more landing room). Then I wait in that flat area to the right of the terminal(you can wait on any surface you like, just don't get killed, and make sure theres a high ceiling) and when the thwump come back at me, I jump over it, let it go under(I usually land on the 45 degree right facing slant to the right of the terminal) , then make the rest of my jumps. I jump from that 45 degree slant to the next small gap in the mines, a smaller slant that faces left, and then I hop (I think it's safer than a full jump) to the small flat gap between mines. Then I hop over to the slanted corner and wait(hop and wait, so I don't fall immediately).

This next part(next 2 corridors) is extremely difficult, and there's no way around it that I found. My favorite way to do it is very hard, but so is every other way. You have to trigger that thwump facing upwards by leaning over the edge or hopping. Then when it hits the top, fall off the ledge under it. There are three slants you can land on, and each has a way to survive.

This is where it gets extremely difficult. You can pick which ledge to land on, I'll explain each, and I'll put a number for each so you can know when I talk about each. I like to land on the ledge on the left (the steepest one), so I'll start by explaining that.
(*1*) When you fall, land directly on the ledge, which will require a little steering, because if you fall straight down, you won't be far enough left to hit it. With the momentum of your fall, jump as soon as you hit the ledge, which is very hard, and then land in the small gap between mines (there's a flat part and a slanted part, but it's tough to land in that area because of the speed). Depending on how fast you were going and where you jump from, you will 9 times out of ten need to hold right to slow down your jump so you don't overshoot that small gap. Then jump immediately when you land to avoid the thwump coming from the left straight at you. You can jump straight up and come back down or you can jump up and left to the next piece of floor clear of mines, which is three mines away from where you landed. From there, just keep jumping from one small clearing to another til you are on that ledge at the end of the corridor(the jumps are hard, I know, but there's nothing I can do to help you with that). *Alternatively*, once you jump over the thwump that comes from the left side towards you, you can wait til it comes back and ride the left side of it to the ledge like I have previously described.
(*2*) Landing on the slant on the far right instead of the slant I talked about earlier is much the same. I don't like it because you have to watch out for the mines to even get to the slant to land on it, and once you land on it, the jump is harder. Anyways, once you land on the small slant on the right, do the exact jump as I described earlier, to the gap between a set of 3 mines and a set of 4 mines. Only now, the jump is farther. I have done this, so I know it is possible, but I think it's harder (personal opinion).
(*3*) The middle ledge. You might think it's easier, because you don't have to jump right when you land on it, and for some it will be. Since you can't jump left with enough speed to beat the thwump coming towards you when you land in the middle, your only choice is to wait for the thwumps to come to you. On the other ledges, you didn't have to worry about when the timing with vertical thwump coming back down, but for this one it may make a big difference. The idea for this ledge is to wait for the vertical thwump to come back down, and jump up and left off your ledge into that little gap between the mine and the vertical thwump before it traps you. If you wait for the vertical thwump at the top of the descent, so that when you fall to this middle ledge, you barely beat the thwump coming back down(so you are pretty close to getting smashed between the corner you fall from and the thwump coming back down), if you do that, what happens is that the vertical thwump is closer to resetting when the thwump coming from the left triggers. This allows you enough time to trigger the vertical thwump again by jumping up and left(you may like to jump to the left-facing 45 degree slant to left of the middle slant to prevent being trapped) and so when that vertical thwump triggers for the second time, the left-right thwump goes underneath you. Then you can either ride that thwump over to the ledge on the left side of the corner, or wait in one of the safe parts and let it go under you, or you can go faster through this horizontal corridor than the thwump does coming back. The point is, if you can delay the thwump coming from the left triggering, it makes this easier, and the basic idea is get the vertical thwump out of the corner and make it so you don't have to deal with that thwump coming fast at you from the left. It's a tricky jump triggering the vertical thwump from that lower right corner so that the left-right thwump doesn't kill you, but you may find it easier than executing the jumps from the other ledges.

Any way you do that last part, it's probably going to be very hard, and you end up on the small ledge on the left part of the corridor. This vertical corridor is small and nothing happens in it, so I recommend gathering your thoughts and focusing for the last part, which is hard. Just jump your way to that top small slant that faces right, and get ready.

The last part is the most intense. You start from that little slant at the start of the corridor(the thwump won't trigger yet, so don't worry). The next jumps are precision jumps that require skill and speed. From that slant, jump to the SECOND gap in the mines (theres a piece of gold over each gap). The second one is MUCH easier to hit for me, and it makes clearing the thwump easy. The thwump triggers as you land, so from that second gap, jump high and to the right a little, and follow the ceiling to land in the last gap in the mines. Then jump high and to the right again, and follow the ceiling again right to the door. Congrats, you made it!
[/easy way]
That's Aries guide. My average post length just went up seven characters

Counter to the tidal deceleration of the Earth, there is a mechanism that is in fact accelerating the rotation. The Earth is not a sphere, but rather an ellipsoid that is flattened at the poles. SLR has shown that this flattening is decreasing. The explanation is, that during the ice age large masses of ice collected at the poles, and depressed the underlying rocks. The ice mass started disappearing over 10000 years ago, but the Earth's crust is still not in hydrostatic equilibrium and is still rebounding (the relaxation time is estimated to be about 4000 years). As a consequence, the polar diameter of the Earth increases, and since the mass and density remain the same, the volume remains the same; therefore the equatorial diameter is decreasing. As a consequence, mass moves closer to the rotation axis of the Earth. This means that its moment of inertia is decreasing. Because its total angular momentum remains the same during this process, the rotation rate increases. This is the well-known effect of a spinning figure skater who spins ever faster as she retracts her arms. From the observed change in the moment of inertia the acceleration of rotation can be computed: the average value over the historical period must have been about −0.6 ms/cy . This largely explains the historical observations.

#292590 2 2007-02-01T22:49:01Z scythe33
One of the biggest mistakes people make with this level is to move slowly after the drones are released. This is wrong; you should move quickly. You want the first drone to chase you towards the place where you got the switch, and you want the second drone to chase you toward the place where the first drone was originally trapped. This will hold them off long enough for you to get away.
The second hard part is getting back up the right wall--again, rather than jump slowly, jump fast, and remember you don't have to be hanging on the wall-just close to it-to jump off of it. It's very hard to get used to, and i should know.
This is the "optimal" route; adjust it if a drone gets in the way.

#310529 359 2007-04-06T23:42:19Z scythe33
Quote: macaddict_17, 2007-04-06T20:00:53Z
1. The rate of decay has remained constant (The good one)
2. The system has remained closed (The bad one)
3. The ratio of daughter to parent in the rock is known (The ugly one)
Just as an example, I'll use uranium-thorium dating:
Uranium salts dissolve in water. Thorium salts do not. Therefore, when a (sedimentary) rock is formed, it contains uranium, but almost no thorium (Thorium is so rare in the Earth's crust that it will not be present in measurable amounts-and not those comparable to radioactive production)
That's 3.
After a rock is formed, uranium and thorium do not leave it-and after uranium has stopped being added to the rock, neither enters. So, with respect to uranium and thorium, the system has remained closed. (Moreover, if uranium did continue to enter the rock, radiometric dating would give too low of an answer, not too high)
Now, the idea that the rate of decay has remained constant-that, I can't fully answer to, but many experiments show that the rate of radioactive decay is somewhat stable.
Moreover, if the average chance for an atom of uranium to give off an alpha particle is "p", and the standard deviation "sigma (all that matters is a finite standard deviation)" (I'm going to assume the normal distribution-if it's not, the Central Limit Theorem predicts that the distro will tend to it over time), the half-life limits to a fixed value over time, with shrinking standard deviation.

#315819 403 2007-04-25T20:51:03Z scythe33
Quote
give an example of a genetic mutation or an evolutionary process which can be seen to increase the information in the genome
Damn, I thought we were done with this argument. Let's say that we have a string of binary:
S = 1000111
Now, a "mutation" would be changing a 0 to a 1 or a 1 to a 0, so there are seven possible "mutations". Let's call them A, B, C, D, E, F, and G.
For each of these mutations, it either increases, decreases, or does not change the "information" in the string, according to any definition you wish to assign. Now, if any mutation increases information, we are done. If any mutation decreases information, say, mutation X, applying it to the string gives string SX. Now if we undo mutation X, call it, say, X', this brings us back to string S, which increased information, and we are done. This leaves us with the idea that either:
-there are mutations that increase "information"
-mutations do not change "information", i.e., "information" is a meaningless concept
*sigh*

What you appear to be disagreeing with, baron, is the Archimedean property of the real numbers.
Naturally, since the real numbers are defined to include that property, we can construct
(let 0.99~ be "t" for this argument)
(1-t) > 0 (since 0.99~ =/= 1)
therefore, for some n,
(1-t)n > 1
n - nt > 1
But for all n,
n * (0.99~) = n-1 + 0.99~
which violates the Archimedean property which is assumed.
If we throw it out, we have constructs like Synthetic differential geometry or Smooth infinitesimal analysis-which are interesting, but useless in practical situations.

An upward-facing one-way (as in, one that acts like a platform) will hold the ninja one pixel higher than will an "E" tile.
So, if you're standing on an "e" tile, the ninja's foot is below the top of the oneway, and he falls through. As for the triple-jump, that was discovered in trib4lmaniac's time.

#346685 149 2007-07-23T22:14:23Z scythe33
To get to Laboratory C, you'll first have to get out of your room. There are a few ways to theoretically do this:
1: If the door is made of wood and the walls aren't, it might be possible to use fire to burn a small hole in the door. Keep lots of wet towels on hand while doing this, as fire will use up air quickly and you don't want any more than you need. The door could be lit by lighting a small piece of deodorant on fire near it.
2: If the door has a window (I recall it does), break the window. The resulting hole will be full of sharp glass, so attempt to knock out as much glass as possible before climbing through.
Personally, I suspect Medea of being an O'Brian. I'd watch for her to slip up, even slightly.
(If both are possible, use #2 over #1. It's far safer.)

#359071 229 2007-08-24T19:54:02Z scythe33
45-3... the route is obvious. How is not. To make it over the floorguard properly, you have to stand under the slope, next to the wall. When you jump, the slope should push you to the right enough to get the switch. Jump right as the floorguard enters the chamber you are in, and jump as low as possible. You don't want to hit the right side of the ceiling; it will slow you down. After you jump, hold right. You should be a good half-inch ahead of the floorguard, which will give you more time than you need to make it out of even the bottom tunnel
The tunnel with the gold is easy. Get it or skip it; your choice (45-4 has ample gold if you start with at least 20 seconds on the clock)
