Quote: Demonz, 2008-06-15T19:25:25Z
You can remove the lens, for instance, and they eye still functions. It doesn't function as well, but some vision is preferable to no vision at all, and so it could have evolved that way.
Not quite. The eye still has some features without which it does not function at all - the cornea, the cones/rods, the optic nerve, the retina. It still needed all those. But I see what you mean.
There was a computer simulation performed to test this theory. Originally, the "eye" was a flat photosensitive membrane, that sent one of two possible messages: "there is light where the membrane points" and "there is no light where the membrane points". This was allowed to "evolve", making only small changes, and eventually reached a dual-lens construction with a sophisticated nerve system not unlike the human eye (the cornea does, in fact, function as a lens).
In ~r fashion, the state of the art agrees that the eye is not irreducibly complex.

Also, in a recent experiment, a strain of E.coli made a genetic shift significant enough to be considered a new species, gaining the previously unheard of ability to metabolize citrate.

As Dave has proven to approximately half the forum, saying marijuana should be legalized is the new Ch t-shirt. Certainly, there's a point, but it's getting clich; take your arguments to your Congressman.
So, let's start with Salvia Divinorum. First off, the main reason it should be legalized is that it's already legal everywhere except Australia. Doing nothing is easy, right, guys? (Trust me, I'm very experienced in that area)
Or, on a more serious note, let's take into account that there's currently little information about it; there are either no cases of serious addiction/overdose or too few for me to find any. See, there are efforts in a few states, and in the UK to ban the stuff, even though there's hardly a case for doing so. One lawmaker was quoted as saying it "may be as dangerous as marijuana and LSD (slight paraphrase)", which to me is hilarious, because neither marijuana nor LSD have significant risks associated with their use. It is, in all fairness, a dissociative, in dangerous company alongside DXM-but just because it produces similar effects doesn't mean it has similar risks. I argue that there should at least be more research done before any action is taken to ban the stuff, and luckily, most scientists in the field seem to agree.

Ibogaine is a different, more complicated story. It's a psychedelic, and like most psychedelics not very addictive. Still, it's illegal-but that's not really the point here. Rather, it seems to stop most drug addictions right in their tracks. Even if not legalized for OTC use, it's incredibly stupid not to at least research the effect and hopefully, put it to use in rehab clinics. It should at the very least be rescheduled, perhaps to Schedule II (I still think that's not enough, but too much change too quickly causes too much public drama).

Shocking, but False

Sometimes it just amazes me how these stories evolve. Let me start off by saying that the Department of Homeland Securitys Science & Technology Directorate nor TSA have been pursuing shock bracelets for airline passengers as alleged by the Washington Times Blog.

This allegation stemmed from a misleading video posted on the Lamberd Website which depicts an ID bracelet that would contain identifying information as well as the ability to stun the wearer. The company claims to connect use of such a device to DHS and TSA, but no discussions between these agencies has ever taken place.

This all originated from a meeting held two years ago with a private company representative (not Lamberd) who proposed bracelet technology in response to the TSA's desire to find less-than-lethal means to detain an apprehended suspect.

The bracelet was never intended to replace boarding passes, contain ID information or be worn by all passengers as asserted in the Lamberd video and discussed in the Washington Times Blog.

The hypothetical use of the bracelet would have been for transporting already apprehended prisoners and detainees at prisons and border patrol facilities, and DHS was looking to see if there were potential air travel applications for apprehended suspects.

This concept was never funded or supported by the DHS or TSA and hasnt even been discussed for two years. The letter circulating throughout the blogosphere from Paul Ruwaldt was not addressed to Lamberd and merely states the DHS was interested in learning more about the technology. #452270 5 2008-07-11T16:08:30Z scythe33
scythe33's rum pie!
A classic, I tell ya.

9-inch pie shell (already baked)
1/2 cup sugar
2 tablespoons cornstarfch
1/2 teaspoon salt
2 cups milk
2 eggs, separated
2 teaspoons unflavored gelatin
3 tablespoons cold water
2 tablespoons rum
1 ounce melted unsweetened chocolate (cool)
1/4 teaspoon cream of tartar.
Stir together 1/2 cup sugar, the cornstarch, and salt in saucepan. Blend milk and egg yolks; stir into sugar mixture. Cook over medium heat, stirring consantly, just until mixture boils. Reserve 1 cup of the custard mixture; set aside.
Soften gelatin in cold water, stir into remaining custard mixture (not the 1 cup reserved, the other part). Stir in rum. Place pan in bowl of ice and water or chill in refrigerator, stirring occasionally, until mixture mounds slightly when dropped from spoon. Combine chocolate and the reserved custard mixture. Pour into baked pie shell.
Beat egg whites and cream of tartar until foamy. Beat in 1/3 cup sugar, 1 tablespoon at a time; continue beating until stiff and glossy. Do not underbeat. Fold remaining custard mixture into meringue. Spread on chocolate mixture. Chill at least 3 hours or until set (overnight is good). If desired, garnish with whipped cream; sprinkle with shaved chocolate.

#452957 4 2008-07-15T04:31:11Z scythe33
Quote: Skyline, July 14, 2008 04:26 pm
The Weather Channel and its cheap jazz music blares. My sister walks in with a disgusted look on her face. Apparently, I stole her turn on the computer. She was playing solitaire for the past two hours. Apparently, I'm a "JERK". APPARENTLY, I CAN'T HEAR HER BITCH ABOUT ME IN THE GODDAMNED ROOM RIGHT NEXT TO ME. Summer.

I have a house on an island in Florida. Which really isn't a bad thing, because I do enjoy it. But when you're trapped down here with your horribly irritating father, your not-so-bad mother, and two boring sisters, it's not as great as it sounds.

So we go to the beach. Again. And again. And again. And goddamned again. Now, the past few weeks haven't been as bad because my older sister came down with her boyfriend, and they were great to hang out with. But with them having recently flown out of here, I'm standing in the sand and staring at my younger sister complaining about whatever the hell she has to complain about. I do admit, I enjoy her company sometimes. But today at the beach, she's afraid to go in the water. Now, the complete isolation from my friends has lead to a lot of growing tension over the past two weeks, so I don't start out being the happiest camper here. But with my family reluctant to do anything but stare at the sand and sit on their asses, I get fed up. This may sound very selfish and unreasonable of me, but as I said, I'm not exactly happy to start out with. So I walk. Away from everyone.

My feet are burning in the sand, but I could care less. I keep walking with my eyes at my feet, and I don't stop until I'm tempted by the ocean. So I go in and swim for a while in the water. This seems to relax me, so I get out and start walking back towards the familiar group of beach umbrellas, only a speck on the horizon. After walking for a bit, my mother's figure appears. She approaches me, and then proceeds immediately to yell at me for going in the water out of her watch. Now, keep in mind, I was in about five feet of ocean with calm waves and no rip tides or any of that shit. I ignore the "you should know better"'s and just walk back to dry off.

I feel lonely. I feel abandoned. I feel like I'm wasting my life. I want adventure, or something exciting. I want a better thrill than going mini golfing, which is as exciting as it seems to get around here. I just want something different. The threat of school and its obligations is looming. I need to work on my saxophone and train for cross country. And of course, summer reading. But all I want to do is just run the fuck away to somewhere else and live without any worries or work, and just do what I enjoy. I throw this idea away, but it still seems to linger in my mind. Basically, this island is driving me to the goddamned brink. Although there isn't anything inherently tragic or bad in my life, I feel like I need to make this post and complain like some self-centered prick. And you know what, that sounds about right. I feel justified. But I'm still not satisfied.

I may post more, but feel free to comment or do whatever you please.

I'm considering driving up to Jacksonville and dragging your ass down here.

#464207 3 2008-08-24T23:11:09Z scythe33
Quote: DemonzLunchBreak, 2008-08-24T08:40:01Z
Pragmatism has a similar kind of issue. The pragmatic theory of truth is that that which is useful to believe is true. People think that this is somehow a separate idea from say, correspondence theory of truth (that which corresponds to reality is true), but that's clearly not true; it's just an unnecessary (and confusing) redefining of the word "truth." When people talk about something being true, typically, they mean what correspondence theory says. It's a semantic trick on the part of the pragmatists to call useful propositions true. Useful propositions are useful. Pragmatists are really people who advocate usefulness over truth. However, they do this in the most confusing way possible, by redefining a word that already has a commonly understood definition.
I couldn't help but think of Bokononism while reading that.
